segments.prompt:
2D hand-drawn cinematic single-character sequence, vertical 9:16, 15 seconds.

STYLE IDENTITY LOCK: preserve the verified drawing language, proportions, materials and original colors of Picture 1 and Picture 2. Keep the exact mouse-eared mutant girl's short white hair with eye-covering fringe and small upward curl, large translucent pale-violet mouse-ear structures, small slender body, oversized pale robe, dark collar, cuffs and hem blocks, diagonal strap and side satchel. Preserve the forest-lake identity and its warm-sky/cool-water color relationship. Reference fidelity overrides generic style wording.

VISUAL EXPRESSION VARIABLE: use restrained readable 2D motion, compatible variable-weight hand-drawn lines, thin watercolor-like shading only where consistent with the references, soft diffuse light, muted shadows and quiet negative space. For this controlled version, clarity comes from a fixed observational frame rather than camera movement or montage.

CHARACTER (Picture 1): show exactly one physical instance of the established mouse-eared mutant girl. If Picture 1 contains multiple identity views, they all describe this one character and must never become multiple people. Preserve her cautious behavior, clothing and accessories.

ENVIRONMENT (Picture 2): preserve the same verified lake, layered forest, spatial continuity and established palette logic of SCENE-02. Picture 2 defines the place, not a mandatory crop. Do not invent a bridge, dock, stones, roots, buildings or props. The water image is only the optical reflection of the same girl, physically dependent on her position and deformed only by the water surface.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: use one fixed medium-wide three-quarter side view for the entire segment. Keep her full route, feet, nearby water and dependent reflection readable together in one frame. Place her on the shore-side third, retain negative space over the lake, preserve one screen axis, and do not push, pan, track, zoom or cut.

ACTION: the girl walks slowly parallel to the shore at a safe distance from the water. Her dependent reflection remains causally aligned beneath and beside her. One small natural ripple crosses the reflected outline and briefly deforms its shape without giving it independent motion. She notices the mismatch, stops, and takes one short half-step back from the water. Hold the entire cause and response in the same fixed frame. Her near mouse-ear structure turns toward the ripple first while her torso, hands and feet stay still; her eyes follow a moment later. End on a clear held pose: she remains present and observant without approaching the water.

AUDIO DESIGN: quiet lake air, faint leaves, soft water movement, robe and strap friction, careful steps and one localized ripple. A thin non-melodic low breath tone tightens at the reflected distortion, falls nearly silent on the half-step back and remains suspended at the cut. Audio clarifies cause, attention order and caution; it does not impose song structure or MV rhythm.

NEGATIVE: no second physical character, duplicate girl, clone, twin, separate water person, autonomous reflection, emerging reflection, independent shadow double, split screen or four-person character sheet; no rabbit ears, ordinary replacement ears, tail, horns, wings, armor, weapon, fitted battle costume or adult muscular body; no complete reflection moving on its own or staying delayed after the ripple; no camera push, pan, tracking, zoom, cutaway, close-up or axis change; no bridge, dock, stones, roots, buildings or props; no splash, fall, run, panic, dance, lip-sync, montage or music-video cutting; no cyan-white energy humanoid, glossy 3D render, hard synthetic digital edges, text, subtitle, logo or watermark.

segments.prompt:
2D hand-drawn cinematic single-character sequence, vertical 9:16, 15 seconds, continuing directly from the selected real ending frame of Segment A.

STYLE IDENTITY LOCK: preserve the same verified Picture 1 identity, drawing language, proportions, materials and original colors, and preserve the same Picture 2 forest-lake identity and warm-sky/cool-water palette logic. Keep the girl's short white hair, fringe, small upward curl, translucent pale-violet mouse-ear structures, small body, oversized pale robe, dark edge blocks, diagonal strap and side satchel exactly consistent with Segment A.

VISUAL EXPRESSION VARIABLE: use restrained readable 2D motion, compatible line-weight variation, reference-consistent thin shading, soft diffuse light, muted shadows and quiet negative space. Keep the same fixed observational grammar from Segment A; two small reversible tests and their pauses must carry the performance without camera emphasis.

CHARACTER (Picture 1): show exactly the same one physical mouse-eared mutant girl from Segment A. Preserve the chosen real A ending pose, clothing state, satchel position and cautious expression. A multi-view reference still represents one identity only.

ENVIRONMENT (Picture 2): remain in the same verified SCENE-02 lakeshore space, with the same lake, layered forest, screen direction, lighting direction and palette relationship. The water image is only the optically dependent reflection of this girl; it must respond to her body and the water surface and never behave as a separate entity. Do not add unverified shore objects or reverse space.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: inherit the exact fixed camera, shot size, camera side, shoreline relation and character position from the selected real Segment A ending. Keep one medium-wide three-quarter side frame showing her feet, both small lateral movements, relevant lake surface and dependent reflection together. Do not move the camera, change lens scale, cut, reframe or cross the axis.

ACTION: after the held ending of Segment A, the girl keeps her upper body quiet and makes one small lateral step away from the water. The dependent reflection shifts with her and settles as the last ripple fades. She pauses long enough to confirm the match. Her ears ease slightly. She then deliberately makes one equally small return step to her original walking line and watches the reflection align again. Hold one calm beat. Without moving closer to the water, she resumes her original slow direction along the shore for two measured steps. End with the reflection causally aligned, her shoulders slightly less tense and her attention curious rather than alarmed.

AUDIO DESIGN: continue the same quiet lake air, faint leaves and soft water ambience, adding two measured robe-softened side steps, subtle strap movement and the fading ripple. Use two very soft non-melodic tonal pulses triggered by the outward and return tests; the second settles into a quiet low release as she resumes walking. Audio supports observation and emotional easing, never song structure or MV rhythm.

NEGATIVE: no second physical character, duplicate girl, clone, twin, separate water person, autonomous reflection, emerging reflection, independent shadow double, split screen or four-person character sheet; no rabbit ears, ordinary replacement ears, tail, horns, wings, armor, weapon, fitted battle costume or adult muscular body; no reflection moving before her, acting independently or remaining delayed after the water settles; no camera push, pan, tracking, zoom, cut, close-up, reframing or axis change; no bridge, dock, stones, roots, buildings, props or reverse space; no approach into water, jump, run, dance, panic, lip-sync, speed ramp, montage or music-video cutting; no cyan-white energy humanoid, glossy 3D render, hard synthetic digital edges, text, subtitle, logo or watermark.
